chunks.text: 72-year-old male, Retired, resident of Ang Mo Kio, Singapore.
History of pneumonia resolved 2 years ago
Remote history of left femur fracture (30 years ago), fully healed
Previous use of Warfarin for atrial fibrillation, discontinued 4 years ago
Prostatectomy (Transurethral Resection of the Prostate, TURP) (elective).
General Anesthesia with Spinal Anesthesia (Combined Spinal-Epidural Anesthesia)

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, sir. I'm Dr. Tan, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your surgery tomorrow. How are you feeling today?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, doctor. I'm okay lah, just a bit nervous about the operation, but I know it's necessary.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's completely normal. Let's go through a few things to make sure we're all set for tomorrow. Can you tell me a bit about your medical history and why you're having this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. I've had trouble with my prostate for a while now — frequent urination, especially at night, and sometimes I can't go at all. The doctor said it's BPH, and now they're doing a TURP to remove some of the enlarged tissue.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. I see from your records that you have hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease. Are these well-controlled with your current medications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. My blood pressure is usually around 130/80, and my sugar levels are okay with Metformin. I also take Lisinopril and Amlodipine for blood pressure, and Dutasteride for the prostate.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Now, regarding your medications — I see you're on Aspirin and Omeprazole. Can you confirm if there have been any changes to your medication list since your last hospital visit, particularly regarding any acid-reducing medications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, yes, doctor. I stopped Omeprazole about six months ago because my gastritis got better. Now I take Pantoprazole 30mg once daily when I feel some stomach discomfort, but not every day.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for letting me know. That's important. Are you allergic to anything, and have you had any reactions to medications or anesthesia in the past?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I'm allergic to penicillin. I had a rash the one time I took it. But I've had surgeries before — hernia repair and cataract — and I didn't have any problems with the anesthesia then.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great, that's helpful. For this surgery, we're planning to use a combination of general and spinal anesthesia — a spinal-epidural technique. This will help with pain control during and after the surgery. Does that sound okay to you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor, whatever is best for the surgery and my condition. I trust your team.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Now, just to confirm — have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. I had my last meal around 7pm last night and only sipped some water this morning, but that was before 6am.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. We'll make sure you're well-hydrated and that your blood sugar is stable before surgery. Is there anything else you'd like to ask or tell me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. I think that's all. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: You're very welcome. We'll see you in the morning, and I'll be there to make sure everything goes smoothly. Take care, and get some rest.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] spinal needle inserted, bupivacaine two point five milligrams, fentanyl ten micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] epidural catheter placed, bupivacaine one milligram test dose

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] iv fluids normal saline one liter bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:30] blood pressure one hundred sixty over one hundred, labetalol twenty milligrams iv

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:00] surgery completed, desflurane off, reversal done, extubated

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Mr. Tan, how are you feeling now after the surgery? Any pain or discomfort?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm feeling okay, Doctor. Got a bit of discomfort here and there, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: On a scale from 0 to 10, how would you rate your pain right now?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe around 3 or 4, lah. It's manageable.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Have you been feeling nauseous or sick to your stomach at all?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, no nausea. I'm a bit thirsty, but that's about it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Are you breathing comfortably? Any tightness or difficulty breathing?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine, Doctor. No problem there.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Did you experience any awareness or discomfort during the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don't remember anything. I was out cold.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Given your hypertension and diabetes, we'll keep a close eye on your vitals and blood sugar levels. Any concerns or questions?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, Doctor. I think that's all. Thank you.

72-year-old male undergoing elective Transurethral Resection of the Prostate (TURP) for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH). He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease (CKD).

The patient is currently controlled on antihypertensive medications with blood pressure around 130/80, and his diabetes is managed with Metformin. He has an allergy to penicillin (rash reaction) but no known reactions to anesthetics. He is NPO since last night and had a combined spinal-epidural anesthesia with general anesthesia for the procedure.

Intra-operatively, the patient received propofol, fentanyl, bupivacaine, and had a blood pressure spike to 160/100, which was treated with labetalol. Surgery was completed without complications, and the patient was extubated after reversal of anesthesia.

Anticipated post-operative issues include hypertension or hypotension due to intra-operative blood pressure fluctuations, glycemic instability due to diabetes and NPO status, increased risk of PONV from opioid use, potential airway complications post-extubation, need for careful analgesia management due to combined spinal-epidural anesthesia, and monitoring for renal function due to stage 3 CKD.

Monitor blood pressure closely and adjust antihypertensive medications as needed. Check blood glucose levels regularly and manage accordingly. Watch for signs of PONV and consider antiemetics. Assess airway and respiratory status post-extubation. Provide adequate analgesia while monitoring for breakthrough pain. Ensure renal function is monitored and maintain fluid balance. Reconcile the patient's PPI use (Pantoprazole) and monitor for gastrointestinal issues.
